To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the EAdi position is affected by PEEP, BP, and IAP, but that the EAdis signal is stable in all tested situations.

PEEP, BP, and IAP may influence EAdi catheters’ positioning, although not compromising the stability of EAdi signal, and the catheter positioning tools are helpful to ensure an optimal catheter positioning.
“Influence of body posture, positive end-expiractory pressure (PEEP), and intra-abdominall pressure on oesophageal catheter position for neurally adjusted ventilation assist (NAVA).”
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of PEEP, body position, intra-abdominal pressures and abdominal surgical belt on catheter positioning for NAVA.
the effects of body positions, PEEP and IAP on the positioning of the oeso-phageal EAdi-catheter.
the question of how to position the oesophageally implanted EAdi catheters in the correct position in order to ensure a stable and reliable electrical activity signal of the diaphragmatic muscle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a stable signal can be achieved in most of the situations tested.
the EAdi is not affected by PEEP or IAP.
the catheter positioning should be re-evaluated when PEEP is changed, the body position is changed, or intra-abdominal pressures are changed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a stable signal is not necessarily an indication for a correct catheter position.
the EAdi is a stable and reproducible signal in all tested situations and that the catheter positioning is affected by the PEEP level, the BP and the IAP.
a stable EAdi signal is not enough to guarantee an optimal catheter positioning.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the optimal EAdi signal should be obtained in the supine position at PEEP 0 cmH2 O.
a stable signal does not necessarily mean an optimal position of the catheter.
the EAdi position may change during NAVA and that this may have an impact on NAVA delivery.
